sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (e.g. 'annual', 'sick', 'emergency') — used in every leave request creation and policy resolution path; is_active: filters active leave types for dropdowns and policy assignment screens

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join path when resolving which policy applies to a leave request; also used in balance calculations; is_active: filters active policies for employee-facing leave type listings and HR configuration screens

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number — used in every employee resolution path; email: unique lookup for login and notification delivery; manager_id: 'my direct reports' queries for manager approval workflows and team views; department: HR filtering and departmental leave calendar views; employment_status: filters active employees for leave eligibility checks

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: primary access pattern — employees list their own leave requests; also used in manager team views; status: filters by status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) for approval queues and dashboards; leave_type_id: filters by leave type for reporting and balance reconciliation; start_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-request detection; end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-request detection; approved_by: lookup for audit trails showing who approved what

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: primary access pattern — employees check their own balances; also used in leave-request validation to check remaining days; policy_id: join path for policy resolution and HR balance reports grouped by policy; fiscal_year: filters balances to the current fiscal year; combined with employee_id for the most frequent query shape; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint index — one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year; also the lookup key during leave request validation

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: primary access pattern — 'show me all changes to leave request X' or 'all changes to employee Y'; action: filters by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE) for compliance reports; performed_by: 'who did what' queries for audit review; performed_at: time-range queries for audit log browsing and retention policies

methods: findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date, excludeId?: string): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, approvedBy?: string, approvedAt?: Date): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findByEmployeeIdPolicyIdAndFiscalYear(employeeId: string, policyId: string, fiscalYear: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
updateUsedDays(id: string, usedDays: number, remainingDays: number): Promise<LeaveBalance>

data_notes: All six tables and six repository interfaces defined. Tables: leave_types (lookup), leave_policies (entitlement rules), employees (with manager FK for approval hierarchy), leave_requests (core entity with status lifecycle), leave_balances (per-employee per-policy per-fiscal-year tracking), audit_logs (GP-002 compliance). Repositories: ILeaveTypeRepository→PgLeaveTypeRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository→PgLeavePolicyRepository, IEmployeeRepository→PgEmployeeRepository, ILeaveRequestRepository→PgLeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository→PgLeaveBalanceRepository, IAuditLogRepository→PgAuditLogRepository — all backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts. Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee-scoped lookups, status filtering for approval queues, fiscal-year + employee composite for balance checks, overlapping date-range detection, and audit entity-type+entity-id lookups.
